body:
Adds `research/reproducible-refereed-training` (MIT, stdlib-only, 10 tests): emulated float32 reduction-order drift, Merkle-committed training trace, teacher-forced one-step referee with tolerance τ, and a short white paper.

Findings: canonical order gives exactly zero drift; relative drift of zero-mean dot products is Cauchy-tailed; state-level drift is a few ulps (a Gaussian model is conservative there); a per-step tolerance is a cumulative hidden-deviation budget (about 7.2·δ in the tested trace). Limitations are stated in the paper. The root README and portfolio page are updated.
